issues.legal_issue: A time-limited tenancy approval is invalid when the landlord obtains it after creating a tenancy but withholds the existing tenancy and possession from the decision-maker.
material_facts: The tenants were placed in joint possession under an oral tenancy before the landlord sought approval for a time-limited tenancy.

A single security payment and advance-rent payment, along with the tenants’ common entry into possession, supported the finding that there was one existing tenancy rather than separate later tenancies.
The landlord sought approval while representing that the premises would not be needed for her own occupation during the proposed term, without disclosing that the tenants were already in possession.
The tenants also made statements supporting the proposed limited term, but the decision-maker was not given the true facts about the earlier tenancy.
issues.conclusion: The approval was obtained by fraud through suppression of relevant facts and was a nullity; it could not support the landlord’s applications to recover possession.
issues.legal_principle: Section 21 of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958 contemplates the creation of tenancy rights after the Rent Controller’s sanction, not post-facto approval of an undisclosed tenancy. The landlord must disclose an existing tenant’s possession and the terms of the tenancy. The Rent Controller must independently apply his mind because the sanction has legal consequences; statements by the parties cannot cure the withholding of relevant facts. The Court relied on S.B. Noronah v. Prem Kumari, Inder Mohan Lal v. Ramesh Khanna, J.R. Vohra v. Indian Export House Pvt. Ltd., and Joginder Kumar Butani v. R.P. Oberai.

rule.if: limited_term_possession_enforcement_case and prior_tenant_already_in_possession and landlord_withheld_prior_tenancy and landlord_claimed_future_nonrequirement and limited_term_permission_granted

predicates.limited_term_possession_enforcement_case: A landlord seeks possession through an enforcement process relying on approval for a time-limited tenancy.
predicates.prior_tenant_already_in_possession: The proposed tenant was already in possession under an earlier tenancy before approval was sought.
predicates.landlord_withheld_prior_tenancy: The landlord did not disclose the earlier tenancy and possession to the decision-maker.
predicates.landlord_claimed_future_nonrequirement: The landlord represented that the premises would not be needed for the landlord’s own occupation during the proposed term.
predicates.limited_term_permission_granted: The decision-maker granted permission for the proposed time-limited tenancy.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks possession by enforcing a time-limited tenancy approval after withholding an existing tenancy and possession while claiming future non-requirement, the approval is void.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s delay in challenging an approval obtained by fraud does not cure the approval’s nullity.
material_facts: The tenants challenged the approval on the ground that the landlord had concealed their existing possession and tenancy from the Rent Controller.
The tenants had agreed before the Rent Controller to statements supporting the limited term and had occupied the premises during that term.
The tenants did not promptly seek to have the approval annulled and raised the issue when resisting the landlord’s possession applications.
issues.conclusion: Delay in challenging the approval, or having used the tenancy arrangement, did not make a sanction void through fraud valid or permit possession to be recovered under it.
issues.legal_principle: The Court distinguished J.R. Vohra v. Indian Export House Pvt. Ltd., Inder Mohan Lal v. Ramesh Khanna, and Joginder Kumar Butani v. R.P. Oberai: those decisions treated delay as relevant to whether a tenant should be summarily evicted, but did not hold that delay cures an approval rendered void by fraud upon the statute.

rule.if: limited_term_possession_enforcement_case and approval_obtained_by_fraud_on_decision_maker and tenant_delayed_challenge and tenant_used_limited_term_arrangement

predicates.limited_term_possession_enforcement_case: A landlord seeks possession through an enforcement process relying on approval for a time-limited tenancy.
predicates.approval_obtained_by_fraud_on_decision_m: The approval was obtained after the landlord fraudulently withheld relevant facts from the decision-maker.
predicates.tenant_delayed_challenge: The tenant did not promptly challenge the approval.
predicates.tenant_used_limited_term_arrangement: The tenant occupied the premises during the period contemplated by the limited-term arrangement.

issues.definition: When a tenant delays challenging and uses an arrangement based on approval obtained by fraud, that delay and use do not cure the approval’s voidness.

issues.legal_issue: Acceptance of a later limited-term tenancy does not imply surrender of an earlier tenancy when the later tenancy depends on a void approval.
material_facts: The tenants had already acquired possession under an earlier oral tenancy before the landlord obtained approval for a limited-term arrangement.
The tenants later agreed to take limited-term tenancy rights under the approval.
The approval was void because it had been obtained by withholding the earlier tenancy from the Rent Controller.
issues.conclusion: The tenants did not impliedly surrender their earlier tenancy rights by agreeing to the later limited-term arrangement.
issues.legal_principle: Under clause (f) of section 111 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, implied surrender may arise from acceptance of a new lease, but not where the new lease does not pass an interest according to the contract. A purported later lease that is void cannot effect surrender of the former tenancy. The Court relied on Doe d. Earl of Egrement v. Courtenay.

rule.if: limited_term_possession_enforcement_case and prior_tenancy_exists and tenant_accepted_limited_term_rights and later_lease_depended_on_void_approval

predicates.limited_term_possession_enforcement_case: A landlord seeks possession through an enforcement process relying on approval for a time-limited tenancy.
predicates.prior_tenancy_exists: The tenant held tenancy rights before the later limited-term arrangement was made.
predicates.tenant_accepted_limited_term_rights: The tenant agreed to take tenancy rights for a limited term under the later arrangement.
predicates.later_lease_depended_on_void_approval: The later lease depended on an approval that was void.

issues.definition: When an existing tenant accepts limited-term rights under a lease dependent on void approval, the acceptance does not imply surrender of the existing tenancy.
